attributes.residual: THE 8 SURPLUS WORDS ARE NOW NAMED, AND THE NAME IS NOT 'deletable'. Relocation-symbol dump, both objects, `fnasm.py game/game/combat.c get_cam_wpos_8002ABE0` with and without --ours: the target's symbol set contains NO gCameraTargets entry, while ours carries gCameraTargets(ADDR16_HA) x4 and gCameraTargets(ADDR16_LO) x4. The target materialises gCameraState once into r31 (0x1c/0x20) and reaches the target array as `addi rN,r31,2576` at all four inlined cam_blocked sites (0xd0, 0x2ec, 0x3e4, 0x4f4). Address arithmetic confirms the two spellings denote the same datum: gCameraTargets .bss 0x80240218 minus gCameraState .bss 0x8023F808 = 0xA10 = 2576, which is CAMERA_STATE_TARGETS_OFF, and someone_will_be_off_screen in this same TU already reaches the array that way. So the residual is a shared-base RE-ATTRIBUTION, not a deletion. WHY IT IS CAPPED ANYWAY: the re-base is correct and it does close the words, but it lengthens the base pointer's live range across the whole 448-instruction function and rescrambles register allocation, and BOTH fine-grained arbiters reject it. The surviving residual after form 3 is ours-only '-1 lfd -4 mr' against target-only '+2 addi': four copies where the target re-derives, plus the one lfd/lfs literal-width word that belongs to the still-blocked anonymous-pool respell. UNPARK CONDITION: a form that supplies the shared base at each of the four inline sites WITHOUT holding one register live across the whole function - e.g. re-deriving the base inside each site from a value already live there - so that the four surplus mr disappear instead of moving.
